headline: Chinese research ships traced undersea-cable routes near Taiwan since May, analysis says
dek: Four Chinese scientific research ships have shown abnormal navigation since May 2026 in waters near Taiwan — sharply slowing, stopping for long periods, or changing course irregularly in areas north and east of Taiwan and in the Bashi Channel to the south — and the points where they slowed/stopped…
sources: ingeniSPACE geospatial-intelligence analysis, via Yomiuri Shimbun, relayed by Seoul Economic Daily; Taiwan Coast Guard Administration surveillance footage cited
fault_line: Research or rehearsal? Routine marine survey vs intelligence preparation to cut Taiwan's internet in a crisis — the tracks are real, the intent is inferred.

sections.what_happened: Four Chinese scientific research ships have shown abnormal navigation since May 2026 in waters near Taiwan — sharply slowing, stopping for long periods, or changing course irregularly in areas north and east of Taiwan and in the Bashi Channel to the south — and the points where they slowed/stopped overlap routes of undersea cables linking Taiwan to Japan, the US, Singapore and the Philippines. ingeniSPACE concludes the ships are collecting information related to undersea fibre-optic cables across a wide expanse of water. Context: 24 undersea cables pass near Taiwan, 14 of them international links to Japan, the US, Singapore and the Philippines; similar movements were detected around Japan and the Philippines. The analysis raises the question whether Beijing is gathering intelligence to sever cables in a Taiwan contingency — that intent is the analysts' inference, not a documented Chinese plan. Taiwan's government forecast cited in the piece expects stepped-up Chinese pressure after the CCP fifth plenum via coast guard, research vessels and maritime militia.
sections.what_verified: Single analysis family relayed by one outlet; Yomiuri Shimbun carries no declared tier in the source registry, so it is reported with attribution and does NOT count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: No Chinese statement on the survey activity in the checked material; no cable damage or severing event is alleged — the severing scenario is analytic inference. Social demand check shows the cable story travelling mainly in Chinese-language Threads posts (Liberty Times, 890 likes) rather than as a verified incident.
sections.why_matters: Taiwan's 14 lifelines: four Chinese ships spent six months tracing the exact seabed where Taiwan's internet lives — map explainer, cable routes vs ship tracks, intent clearly labelled as analysis, not fact.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (Yomiuri Shimbun Nov 4, via Seoul Economic Daily): Chinese research ships traced undersea-cable routes near Taiwan since May, analysis says
